'''Papa''' ("'''Baba'''") '''Ababacar Niang Miller''' (born February 7, 2004) is a Spanish professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played in the youth squads of [[Real Madrid Baloncesto]], after which he moved to the U.S. to play [[college basketball]] for [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State University]], [[Florida Atlantic Owls men's basketball|Florida Atlantic University]] and [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]].

== Early life ==
Miller was born on February 7, 2004, in [[Palma de Mallorca]], in the [[Balearic Islands]] in Spain.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/5075626 |publisher=[[ESPN]]|title=Baba Miller|access-date=2026-08-21}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://seminoles.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/baba-miller/6480|publisher=[[Florida State Seminoles]]|title=Baba Miller}}</ref> He has Senegalese and British ancestry.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite news|url=https://en.as.com/ncaa/real-madrid-lose-youth-team-pearl-baba-miller-to-florida-state-n/|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|title=Real Madrid lose youth team pearl Baba Miller to Florida State|date=June 12, 2022|last1=Maestre, Mike |last2=Hall, Andy}}</ref> He began playing as a youth for [[CB Bahía San Agustín]] of Mallorca and later moved to [[Madrid]] to play for [[Distrito Olímpico]].<ref name="auto2"/> At age 12, he joined [[Real Madrid Baloncesto]] and played with the organization through the 2021–22 season.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/wake-forest/basketball/baba-miller-florida-states-mystery-freshman|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Baba Miller: Florida State's Mystery Freshman|date=January 11, 2023|last=Conroy, Ben}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2022/06/06/fsu-basketball-lands-commitment-real-madrid-forward-baba-miller/7532620001/|newspaper=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]|title=Florida State men's basketball lands pledge from top international prospect Baba Miller|date=June 6, 2022|last=Karels, Carter}}</ref> Starting with the youth B team, he played through all the team categories and was promoted to the senior team in December 2021, making his [[EuroLeague]] debut in a 71–65 win over [[PBC CSKA Moscow]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gigantes.com/liga-endesa/baba-miller/|website=Gigantes.com|title=El canterano Baba Miller, inscrito por el Real Madrid para el partido ante el CSKA. Así juega la perla de la cantera blanca (vídeo)|date=December 22, 2021|language=Spanish}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cope.es/emisoras/illes-balears/baleares/mallorca/deportes-mallorca/noticias/baba-miller-debuta-con-primer-equipo-del-real-madrid-euroliga-20211224_1696779|website=[[Cadena COPE|COPE]]|title=Baba Miller debuta con el primer equipo del Real Madrid en la Euroliga|date=December 24, 2021|language=Spanish|last=Jiménez, Jordi}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/basketball/nba/2023/01/11/63be8960ca4741db158b457c.html|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|title=Baba Miller: The enigmatic Spaniard who is ranked Top-10 in the NBA Draft without having made NCAA debut|date=November 1, 2022|last=Corbella, Enrique}}</ref> He was a member of Real Madrid's winning team in the [[2020–21 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] and averaged 11.3 points and 5.3 rebounds per game with the [[Real Madrid Baloncesto B|Real Madrid B Team]] in 2021–22.<ref name="auto2"/><ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/prospect-profiles/nba-draft-scouting-report-florida-states-baba-miller#gid=ci02aa0481f00025c7&pid=usatsi_20165808|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=NBA Draft Scouting Report: Florida State's Baba Miller|date=August 30, 2022}}</ref>

== College career ==
Miller decided to move to the United States and play for a team in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) in 2022, stating that he thought it was best for his development.<ref name="auto2"/> Considered one of the top international prospects, he committed to play for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]] over the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/gonzaga/basketball/miller-commits-to-fsu|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=It's Florida State over Gonzaga for Spanish prospect Baba Miller|last=Ali, Asher|date=June 6, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/34047241|publisher=[[ESPN]]|title=Top international basketball prospect Baba Miller commits to Florida State Seminoles|last=Givony, Jonathan|date=June 6, 2022}}</ref> Prior to the start of the season, Miller was suspended by the NCAA, initially for the entire year but later for 16 games, due to him having received [[US$]]3,000 in third-party money to attend a training camp in 2020; his family paid the money back once they learned that it violated NCAA rules, but the suspension was upheld, drawing widespread criticism.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/fsu/basketball/the-ncaas-last-stand-detailing-the-unjust-suspension-of-baba-miller|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=The NCAA's Last Stand: detailing the unjust suspension of Baba Miller|last=Veazey, Austin|date=November 3, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2022/11/05/fsu-coach-leonard-hamilton-baba-miller-situation-we-going-move-on/10648662002/|newspaper=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]|title=Florida State men's basketball: Leonard Hamilton assesses Baba Miller situation, team before season|last=Karels, Carter|date=November 5, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-stuart-news/135903579/|newspaper=[[The Stuart News]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=January 11, 2023|page=C5|title=Freshman Miller to make debut for FSU at Wake Forest|last=Kassim, Ehsan}} {{Open access}}</ref> He made his return from suspension against the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]], scoring four points and having four rebounds in a 90–75 loss.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://en.as.com/ncaa/baba-miller-makes-ncaa-debut-after-lengthy-suspension-n/|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|title=Baba Miller makes NCAA debut after lengthy suspension|date=January 12, 2023}}</ref> He finished the season with 15 games played while averaging 4.3 points and 3.7 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://floridastate.rivals.com/news/baba-miller-plans-return-to-fsu|website=[[Rivals.com]]|title=Baba Miller wants to 'try to make things right' at FSU in return|date=April 14, 2023}}</ref>

Miller announced in April 2023 that he was returning for his [[sophomore]] season at Florida State rather than declaring for the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2023/04/14/fsu-mens-basketball-baba-miller-plans-to-return-to-seminoles/70115479007/|newspaper=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]|title=Forward Baba Miller plans to return to Florida State men's basketball for sophomore season|last=Kassim, Ehsan|date=April 14, 2023}}</ref>

In May 2024, Miller announced he was withdrawing from the NBA draft and that he would be transferring to [[Florida Atlantic Owls|Florida Atlantic University]].<ref name="datilus 2026">{{cite news |last1=Datilus |first1=Mikai |title=Men's Basketball: Two former Owls to the NBA, one drafted; one signed as an undrafted free agent |url=https://www.upressonline.com/2026/06/mens-basketball-two-owl-alumni-to-the-nba-one-drafted-one-signed-as-an-undrafted-free-agent/ |access-date=2 July 2026 |work=FAU University Press |date=June 26, 2026}}</ref> Miller averaged 11 points, seven rebounds and three assists during the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25 season]] with the Owls, and was selected to the All-American Athletic Conference team.<ref name="datilus 2026"></ref>

Miller transferred to [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]] for the 2025-2026 season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tuckerman |first1=Spencer |title=Men's Basketball Signs Baba Miller |url=https://gobearcats.com/news/2025/05/19/mens-basketball-signs-baba-miller |website=University of Cincinnati Athletics |access-date=2 July 2026}}</ref> With the Bearcats, Miller led the [[Big 12 Conference]] in rebounds and became the first player since [[Oscar Robertson]] to lead Cincinnati in points, rebounds and assists in the same season. After the season, he was named to All-Big 12 Second Team and Big 12 All-Newcomer Team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-09 |title=2026 Phillips 66 All-Big 12 Men’s Basketball Awards Unveiled |url=http://big12sports.com/news/2026/3/9/2026-phillips-66-all-big-12-mens-basketball-awards-unveiled.aspx |access-date=2026-08-29 |website=big12sports.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
On June 24, 2026, Miller was selected by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] with the 36th overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |title=LA CLIPPERS SELECT BABA MILLER 36TH OVERALL IN 2026 NBA DRAFT |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-select-baba-miller-36th-overall-in-2026-nba-draft |website=NBA.com |access-date=2026-08-21 |language=en|date=2026-06-24}}</ref>

== International career ==
Miller played for the [[Spain men's national under-18 basketball team]], including at the [[2021 FIBA U18 European Challengers]] tournament where he averaged 11.8 points, 4.4 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game.<ref name="auto"/> In 2023, he was a member of the [[Spain men's national under-19 basketball team|national under-19 team]] that won the [[2023 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]], starting in the finals and recording 11 points scored and five rebounds in the game, while having an average of 9.4 points and 6.0 rebounds in the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://floridastate.rivals.com/news/baba-miller-enjoys-gold-medal-run-experience-earned-with-spanish-team|website=[[Rivals.com]]|title=Baba Miller enjoys gold medal run, experience earned with Spanish team|date=July 11, 2023|last=Ferrante, Bob}}</ref>
